library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

Liu et al. (2019, *CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology*) use the
deuterium oxide (D2O) dose-to-the-mother technique to classify mother-infant
pairs as exclusively breastfeeding (EBF) or not, and search for a sampling
design shorter than the standard 14-day, seven-sample protocol. The kinetic
model is the one the same authors developed earlier on 113 Indonesian pairs
(Liu et al. 2019, *J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn*, packaged as
`Liu_2019_deuterium`): two linked one-compartment models, the mother losing
D2O at a total rate constant `kmm`, part of which is the lactation clearance
`CLmb` into the infant, and the infant losing it through its own water
clearance `CLbo`; the infant volume is computed from infant weight. In this
paper the model is refitted to 565 pairs pooled from nine countries, with a
combined residual error that differs by country, maternal weight on the
maternal volume and infant weight on the infant clearance. The re-estimated
covariate exponents differ from the earlier fit (0.46 against 0.62 on `Vm`;
0.55 against 0.17 on `CLbo`).

The design search itself (which pairs of sampling days classify pairs as
the full design does; the answer is one sample on days 7-9 and one on days
13-14, paper Table 4) depends on fitting each pair's data and is not part of
the packaged model.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2019b_deuterium"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2019b_deuterium"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12428> (open access; eight
  supplementary files, including the base-model posterior in Supplementary
  Material S3 and each pair's posterior means in Supplementary Material S5).

# Population

The model-building data set has 565 mother-infant pairs and 6485 observations:
the whole calibration study of exclusively breastfeeding pairs in Indonesia
(113 pairs) and two-thirds of a composite of field studies in South Africa,
Thailand, Kenya, Sri Lanka, India, Guatemala, Ghana and Chile, whose
breastfeeding status was not controlled (paper Data; Table 1). Two pairs were
excluded as outliers. Mothers were 26 years old (interquartile range 21-31)
and weighed 56 kg (50-64). Infants were 3.4 months old (2.9-5.4) and weighed
6.2 kg (5.5-7.2) at the start and 6.5 kg (5.8-7.4) at the end of the study;
36% were female, 36% male and 27% of unrecorded sex. Mothers took a single
oral dose of D2O, median 30 g (6-60 g); saliva was assayed by FTIR in 71% and
IRMS in 29% of pairs. By the posterior probability of non-milk water intake
above 86.6 g/day, 187 of the 565 pairs (33%) were classified as not
exclusively breastfed (Table 2).

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: `d/dt(central) = -kmm * central`; `d/dt(infant_central) = kmb * central - kbo * infant_central` | -- | Supplementary Material S1 Eqs. 1-2 |
| `kmb = CLmb / Vm`, `kbo = CLbo / Vb` | -- | S1 Eqs. 5-6 |
| Infant volume `Vb = 1.041 * exp(-0.427 + 0.963 * log(WT_INFANT))` | -- | S1 Eq. 17 (TBW); factor 1.041 from the upstream paper (Eq. A1.10) and its Stan code |
| `Cc = 1000 * central / Vm`, `Cinfant = 1000 * infant_central / Vb` (g to mg/L) | -- | upstream Stan code `amt*1000/Vm` |
| `lvc` (Vm at maternal weight 70 kg) | 3.54 (34.5 L) | Eq. 6 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.46 | Eq. 6 |
| `lcl_infant` (CLbo at infant weight 5 kg) | -0.16 (0.852 L/day) | Eq. 7 |
| `e_wt_infant_cl_infant` | 0.55 | Eq. 7 |
| `lkel` (kmm) | -2.17 (0.114 1/day) | S3 Table S2, base-model posterior (Table 3 prints -2.18) |
| `lcl_milk` (CLmb) | -0.36 (0.698 L/day) | S3 Table S2, base-model posterior |
| `etalvc`, `etalcl_infant` variances | 0.12^2, 0.17^2 | Eqs. 6-7, SD of the intercept |
| `etalkel`, `etalcl_milk` variances | 0.18^2, 0.31^2 | S3 Table S2 and Table 3, "BSV mean" |
| IIV correlations | not reported, 0 | S1 Eqs. 8-13 (LKJ prior) |
| Residual error: combined (Eq. 2), sigma by country | not reported, held at 0 | Results, Model building and selection; S4 Table S3 |
| `Rs` mass balance (vignette only) | -- | S1 Eqs. 14-20 |

# Typical values against the individual posterior means

The paper prints final-model population means only for the two parameters
that carry covariates (Eqs. 6-7). For `kmm` and `CLmb` the packaged values are
the posterior of the base model fitted to the same 565 pairs (Supplementary
Material S3, Table S2). Supplementary Material S5 lists, for each of the 565
pairs, the final-model posterior mean of the four log-scale parameters
*before* the covariate effects are applied (`phi` in the Stan code). Their
averages are therefore an independent estimate of the four population means of
the final model, and their spread a (shrunken) estimate of the between-subject
SDs. The rows of S5 are numbered as the pairs in Figure 2: pair 2 has
`Rs` 58 g/day and is labelled EBF, pair 31 has 734 g/day and is labelled
non-EBF.

```{r typical-values}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Liu_2019b_deuterium"))
ini_df <- mod$iniDf
th <- setNames(ini_df$est, ini_df$name)

# Supplementary Material S5: mean and SD over the 565 pairs of the individual
# posterior means of phi[, 1:4] (log Vm, log kmm, log CLmb, log CLbo), and the
# arithmetic mean and median of the individual posterior means of Rs.
s5 <- data.frame(
  parameter = c("log Vm", "log kmm", "log CLmb", "log CLbo"),
  model_mu = c(th[["lvc"]], th[["lkel"]], th[["lcl_milk"]], th[["lcl_infant"]]),
  model_sd = sqrt(c(th[["etalvc"]], th[["etalkel"]], th[["etalcl_milk"]], th[["etalcl_infant"]])),
  s5_mean = c(3.563, -2.168, -0.357, -0.158),
  s5_sd = c(0.094, 0.178, 0.313, 0.153)
) |>
  mutate(diff_mu = model_mu - s5_mean)
knitr::kable(
  s5 |>
    rename(
      "Parameter" = parameter,
      "Packaged mu" = model_mu,
      "S5 mean of posterior means" = s5_mean,
      "Difference (log)" = diff_mu,
      "Packaged BSV SD" = model_sd,
      "S5 SD of posterior means" = s5_sd
    ),
  digits = 3
)
# The printed values carry two decimals (+/- 0.005); the S5 averages are means
# of 565 shrunken posterior means. Measured: |difference| <= 0.023 (log Vm).
stopifnot(all(abs(s5$diff_mu) < 0.03))
# Posterior means are shrunk toward mu, so their SD can only fall short of the
# BSV SD; for kmm and CLmb shrinkage is negligible.
stopifnot(all(s5$s5_sd <= s5$model_sd + 0.005))
```

All four packaged population means agree with the S5 averages to within the
printed rounding, which supports both the use of the base-model `kmm` and
`CLmb` (no covariate acts on them) and the reading of the intercept SD in
Eqs. 6-7 as the between-subject SD.

A second consistency check uses the covariate equations. The base model has
no covariates, so its log `Vm` and log `CLbo` describe the cohort's median
mother and infant; Eqs. 6-7 evaluated at the Table 1 medians (56 kg; infant
average weight (6.2 + 6.5) / 2 = 6.35 kg) should land on them.

```{r covariate-check}
lvm_at_median <- th[["lvc"]] + th[["e_wt_vc"]] * log(56 / 70)
lclbo_at_median <- th[["lcl_infant"]] + th[["e_wt_infant_cl_infant"]] * log(6.35 / 5)
cov_chk <- data.frame(
  parameter = c("log Vm", "log CLbo"),
  final_at_median = c(lvm_at_median, lclbo_at_median),
  base_model = c(3.45, -0.05)
)
knitr::kable(
  cov_chk |>
    rename("Parameter" = parameter, "Eqs. 6-7 at Table 1 median" = final_at_median,
           "Base model (Table S2)" = base_model),
  digits = 3
)
# Measured: 3.437 vs 3.45 and -0.029 vs -0.05.
stopifnot(all(abs(cov_chk$final_at_median - cov_chk$base_model) < 0.05))
```

# Typical profiles and Figure 2

Figure 2 of the paper shows individual fits for nine pairs, one per country,
each with its own dose (and hence enrichment scale). In every panel the
maternal enrichment falls monoexponentially, the infant's peaks around days
4-6, and the two curves cross between about day 8 and day 12 or converge by
day 14. For the Indonesian calibration pair (number 120, 30 g) the maternal
enrichment starts near 1100-1200 mg/L and falls to about 250 mg/L by day 14,
and the infant's rises to about 500 mg/L around days 5-6. The figure
below shows the typical pair of this model after a 30 g dose (maternal weight
56 kg, infant growing from 6.2 to 6.5 kg) with the 95% between-subject band of
200 simulated pairs.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190703)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190703)
n_pairs <- 200

# Reject-and-redraw inside the Table 1 interquartile-based plausible range; a
# clamp would pile mass on the boundaries.
draw_lnorm <- function(n, median, sdlog, lo, hi) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- exp(rnorm(n, log(median), sdlog))
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}
pairs <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_pairs),
  WT = draw_lnorm(n_pairs, 56, 0.18, 35, 100),
  wt_start = draw_lnorm(n_pairs, 6.2, 0.20, 3.5, 10)
) |>
  mutate(wt_end = wt_start + 0.3)

typical_events <- function(mwt, wt_start, wt_end, t_end = 14, dt = 0.125, dose = 30) {
  obs_t <- seq(0, t_end, by = dt)
  rbind(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = obs_t, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    mutate(WT = mwt, WT_INFANT = wt_start + (wt_end - wt_start) * time / t_end)
}

mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, typical_events(56, 6.2, 6.5),
                           covsInterpolation = "linear", returnType = "data.frame")

# Both outputs are returned on every observation row; dvid = 1 keeps those
# rows on the maternal state rather than letting rxode2 map them to an
# endpoint slot.
obs_t <- seq(0, 14, by = 0.25)
ev_cohort <- bind_rows(
  pairs |> mutate(time = 0, amt = 30, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
  tidyr::crossing(pairs, time = obs_t) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  mutate(WT_INFANT = wt_start + (wt_end - wt_start) * time / 14) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dvid, WT, WT_INFANT)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_cohort, covsInterpolation = "linear",
                       returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r fig2, fig.cap = "Typical-pair and between-subject profiles in the style of Figure 2 of Liu 2019b: maternal (upper at day 0) and infant (lower at day 0) saliva D2O enrichment after a 30 g oral dose to the mother. Lines: typical pair (maternal weight 56 kg, infant 6.2 to 6.5 kg); band: 2.5th-97.5th percentiles of 200 simulated pairs."}
band <- sim |>
  select(id, time, Cc, Cinfant) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cinfant), names_to = "member", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(member, time) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(conc, 0.025), hi = quantile(conc, 0.975), .groups = "drop")
typ <- sim_typ |>
  select(time, Cc, Cinfant) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cinfant), names_to = "member", values_to = "conc")
member_lab <- c(Cc = "Mother", Cinfant = "Infant")

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = band, aes(time, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = member), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = typ, aes(time, conc, colour = member), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_discrete(labels = member_lab) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = member_lab) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "D2O concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig2-checks}
c0 <- sim_typ$Cc[sim_typ$time == 0]
c14 <- sim_typ$Cc[sim_typ$time == 14]
t_peak_inf <- sim_typ$time[which.max(sim_typ$Cinfant)]
c_peak_inf <- max(sim_typ$Cinfant)
t_cross <- sim_typ$time[which(sim_typ$time > 1 & sim_typ$Cinfant >= sim_typ$Cc)[1]]
c(c0 = c0, c14 = c14, t_peak_infant = t_peak_inf, c_peak_infant = c_peak_inf,
  t_cross = t_cross)
# Deterministic typical pair; bounds are the reading of the Figure 2 panels.
stopifnot(
  c0 > 850, c0 < 1250,
  c14 > 150, c14 < 350,
  t_peak_inf >= 4, t_peak_inf <= 7,
  c_peak_inf > 300, c_peak_inf < 600,
  t_cross >= 7, t_cross <= 12
)
```

The typical pair starts at `r round(c0)` mg/L and reaches `r round(c14)` mg/L
at day 14; the infant peaks at `r round(c_peak_inf)` mg/L on day
`r t_peak_inf`, and the curves cross on day `r t_cross`. The timing matches
the Figure 2 panels. Pair 120 sits above the typical pair on both curves: its
mother starts about 20% higher, i.e. has a smaller volume, and since the
infant's input is `CLmb / Vm` times the maternal amount, its infant peak is
higher too (about 500 against `r round(c_peak_inf)` mg/L); both lie inside the
between-subject band.

# Structural check: ODE against the closed form

Supplementary Material S1 gives the analytic solution of the model (Eqs. 3-4),
which the Stan code evaluates with the infant volume taken at each
observation time. For a constant infant weight the packaged ODEs must agree
with it to integrator precision.

```{r closed-form}
closed_form <- function(time, dose, mwt, wt_infant, p) {
  vm <- exp(p[["lvc"]]) * (mwt / 70)^p[["e_wt_vc"]]
  kmm <- exp(p[["lkel"]])
  clmb <- exp(p[["lcl_milk"]])
  clbo <- exp(p[["lcl_infant"]]) * (wt_infant / 5)^p[["e_wt_infant_cl_infant"]]
  vb <- 1.041 * exp(-0.427 + 0.963 * log(wt_infant))
  data.frame(
    time = time,
    Cc = dose * 1000 / vm * exp(-kmm * time),
    Cinfant = dose * 1000 / vm * clmb / (vb * (kmm - clbo / vb)) *
      (exp(-clbo / vb * time) - exp(-kmm * time))
  )
}
sim_const <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, typical_events(56, 6.35, 6.35),
                             rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, returnType = "data.frame")
cf_const <- closed_form(sim_const$time, 30, 56, 6.35, th)
late <- sim_const$time >= 0.5
err_const <- max(abs(c(sim_const$Cc[late] / cf_const$Cc[late] - 1,
                       sim_const$Cinfant[late] / cf_const$Cinfant[late] - 1)))
err_const
stopifnot(err_const < 1e-6)
```

# Non-compartmental analysis

The paper reports no NCA, so the PKNCA results for the typical pair (constant
infant weight, followed for 120 days so that the infant's terminal phase,
which runs at the slower maternal rate, is established) are checked against
the model's closed forms: for the mother `t1/2 = log(2) / kmm` and
`AUC0-inf = 1000 * Dose / (Vm * kmm)`; for the infant every gram that leaves
the mother through milk (`Dose * CLmb / (Vm * kmm)`) is cleared by `CLbo`, so
`AUC0-inf = 1000 * Dose * CLmb / (Vm * kmm * CLbo)`.

```{r nca-typical}
sim_long <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, typical_events(56, 6.35, 6.35, t_end = 120, dt = 0.25),
                            rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, returnType = "data.frame")
# A single-subject solve returns no id column.
conc_long <- sim_long |>
  mutate(id = 1L) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, Cinfant) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cinfant), names_to = "member", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(conc = pmax(conc, 0))
dose_long <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, dose = 30, member = c("Cc", "Cinfant"))
nca_long <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_long, conc ~ time | member + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_long, dose ~ time | member + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))

vm_t <- exp(th[["lvc"]]) * (56 / 70)^th[["e_wt_vc"]]
kmm_t <- exp(th[["lkel"]])
clmb_t <- exp(th[["lcl_milk"]])
clbo_t <- exp(th[["lcl_infant"]]) * (6.35 / 5)^th[["e_wt_infant_cl_infant"]]
expected <- data.frame(
  member = c("Cc", "Cc", "Cinfant", "Cinfant"),
  PPTESTCD = c("aucinf.obs", "half.life", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"),
  expected = c(30000 / (vm_t * kmm_t), log(2) / kmm_t,
               30000 * clmb_t / (vm_t * kmm_t * clbo_t), log(2) / kmm_t)
)
nca_cmp <- as.data.frame(nca_long$result) |>
  inner_join(expected, by = c("member", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / expected - 1))
knitr::kable(
  nca_cmp |>
    mutate(member = member_lab[member]) |>
    select(member, PPTESTCD, PPORRES, expected, pct_diff) |>
    rename("Dyad member" = member, "NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD,
           "PKNCA" = PPORRES, "Closed form" = expected, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff),
  digits = 3
)
# Deterministic typical-pair solve against its own closed form.
stopifnot(all(abs(nca_cmp$pct_diff) < 2))
```

Over the 14-day protocol, the NCA of the virtual cohort by dyad member is:

```{r nca-cohort}
conc_cohort <- sim |>
  select(id, time, Cc, Cinfant) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cinfant), names_to = "member", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(conc = pmax(conc, 0))
dose_cohort <- tidyr::crossing(id = pairs$id, member = c("Cc", "Cinfant")) |>
  mutate(time = 0, dose = 30)
nca_cohort <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_cohort, conc ~ time | member + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_cohort, dose ~ time | member + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 14, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
nca_sum <- as.data.frame(nca_cohort$result) |>
  group_by(member, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), p05 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05),
            p95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(member = member_lab[member])
knitr::kable(
  nca_sum |>
    rename("Dyad member" = member, "NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD,
           "Median" = median, "5th percentile" = p05, "95th percentile" = p95),
  digits = 2
)
```

# Water intake from non-milk sources (Rs)

Supplementary Material S1 (Eqs. 14-20) turns the two clearances into the
infant's water intake from sources other than breast milk, `Rs`, the quantity
on which pairs are classified (non-EBF when the posterior probability of
`Rs > 86.6 g/day` exceeds 0.9). With all quantities in L/day:
breast-milk intake `M = CLmb / 0.889`; water from oxidising milk solids
`Rm = 0.07733 * M`; infant water output corrected for fractionation
`Rcbo = CLbo / 0.9906`; water retained for growth `Rg = (TBW_end -
TBW_start) / 14`; atmospheric water `Ra = 0.063 * (Rcbo + Rg)`; and
`Rs = Rcbo + Rg - CLmb - Rm - Ra`, reported in g/day. The milk-composition,
fractionation and atmospheric constants are sampled from priors in the paper
and held at their means here.

```{r rs}
tbw <- function(wt) exp(-0.427 + 0.963 * log(wt))
rs_calc <- function(cl_milk, cl_infant, wt_start, wt_end, days = 14) {
  m_milk <- cl_milk / 0.889
  rm <- 0.07733 * m_milk
  rcbo <- cl_infant / 0.9906
  rg <- (tbw(wt_end) - tbw(wt_start)) / days
  ra <- 0.063 * (rcbo + rg)
  1000 * (rcbo + rg - cl_milk - rm - ra)
}

# CLbo at the infant's average study weight, i.e. day 7 under linear growth.
rs_pairs <- sim |>
  filter(abs(time - 7) < 1e-8) |>
  select(id, cl_milk, cl_infant) |>
  inner_join(pairs, by = "id") |>
  mutate(Rs = rs_calc(cl_milk, cl_infant, wt_start, wt_end))
rs_typ <- rs_calc(clmb_t, clbo_t, 6.2, 6.5)

# Rs is linear in CLmb and CLbo, so the population mean for the median infant
# is the mass balance at the arithmetic-mean clearances exp(mu + omega^2 / 2).
rs_popmean <- rs_calc(exp(th[["lcl_milk"]] + th[["etalcl_milk"]] / 2),
                      exp(th[["lcl_infant"]] + th[["etalcl_infant"]] / 2) *
                        (6.35 / 5)^th[["e_wt_infant_cl_infant"]],
                      6.2, 6.5)
# Sensitivity of Rs to 0.1 kg of average infant weight.
rs_per_100g <- rs_typ - rs_calc(clmb_t, exp(th[["lcl_infant"]]) *
                                  (6.25 / 5)^th[["e_wt_infant_cl_infant"]], 6.1, 6.4)

rs_summary <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "Typical pair",
    "Population mean, median infant",
    "Simulated cohort mean",
    "Simulated cohort median",
    "Simulated cohort, fraction above 86.6 g/day"
  ),
  value = c(rs_typ, rs_popmean, mean(rs_pairs$Rs), median(rs_pairs$Rs),
            mean(rs_pairs$Rs > 86.6)),
  s5 = c(NA, NA, 145.2, 79.9, 261 / 565)
)
knitr::kable(
  rs_summary |>
    rename("Rs (g/day)" = quantity, "This model" = value,
           "S5 individual posterior means" = s5),
  digits = 2
)
```

```{r rs-checks}
# The simulated cohort must agree with the model's own expectation for the
# cohort's weights; 4 Monte-Carlo standard errors.
rs_cohort_expected <- mean(rs_calc(
  exp(th[["lcl_milk"]] + th[["etalcl_milk"]] / 2),
  exp(th[["lcl_infant"]] + th[["etalcl_infant"]] / 2) *
    ((pairs$wt_start + pairs$wt_end) / 2 / 5)^th[["e_wt_infant_cl_infant"]],
  pairs$wt_start, pairs$wt_end
))
stopifnot(abs(mean(rs_pairs$Rs) - rs_cohort_expected) <
            4 * sd(rs_pairs$Rs) / sqrt(nrow(rs_pairs)))
```

The paper publishes no population summary of `Rs` for this fit. Its
population mean for the median infant, `r round(rs_popmean, 1)` g/day, is
close to the mean of the 565 individual posterior means in S5, 145.2 g/day.
The S5 column summarises the 565 pairs' individual posterior means (mean 145.2, median
79.9 g/day; 261 pairs with a posterior mean above 86.6 g/day, against the 187
that Table 2 classifies as non-EBF by the stricter 90% posterior-probability
criterion). `Rs` is the small
difference between the infant's water turnover and its milk-water intake, so
it is very sensitive to the clearances and to infant weight: each 0.1 kg of
average infant weight moves the typical value by about
`r round(rs_per_100g, 1)` g/day. The simulated cohort also omits the
correlation between `CLmb` and `CLbo`, which the paper fitted but did not
report (the S5 posterior means of the two are correlated at 0.53), and so
overstates the between-pair spread of `Rs`. These numbers are shown for
orientation and are not used to validate the model.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **kmm and CLmb from the base model.** The paper prints final-model
  population values only for `Vm` and `CLbo` (Eqs. 6-7). `kmm` and `CLmb`
  carry no covariates, and their log-scale means and between-subject SDs are
  taken from the base-model posterior on the same 565 pairs (Supplementary
  Material S3, Table S2). Table S2 gives `ln(kmm)` = -2.17 and the main-text
  Table 3, describing the same posterior, -2.18; -2.17 is used, matching the
  S5 average of -2.168. The S5 averages confirm all four population means of
  the final model to within 0.03 on the log scale.
* **Between-subject SD reading.** In Eqs. 6-7, `N(mean, SD)` on the intercept
  is read as the between-subject SD on the log scale, as in the authors'
  earlier paper, whose corresponding SD equals its tabulated BSV. The S5
  spread of individual posterior means (0.094 and 0.153, shrunk) is
  consistent with 0.12 and 0.17.
* **Residual error not reported.** The final model has a combined error whose
  SDs differ by country (one assay method per country). The values are not
  printed in the paper or its supplements, so the residual error is held at
  zero and simulations are of the true saliva enrichment. rxode2 needs a
  separate pair per endpoint, so the model carries `propSd`/`addSd` and
  `propSd_Cinfant`/`addSd_Cinfant`; country is listed as an excluded
  covariate.
* **IIV correlations not reported.** The full 4 x 4 LKJ correlation matrix
  was estimated, but no correlation is printed; all are set to zero. In the
  S5 individual posterior means, `log(CLmb)` and `log(CLbo)` are correlated at
  0.53 and the other pairs at -0.07 to 0.13.
* **Structure from the earlier paper.** The paper refers to its Supplementary
  Material S4 for the Stan code, but S4 contains the model-selection table; the
  code is in the supplement of the earlier paper (Liu et al. 2019, J
  Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn). The equations of S1 (Eqs. 1-6, 17) match it.
  The factor 1.041 relating infant volume to total body water (non-aqueous
  isotope exchange) is not restated in this paper and is taken from the
  earlier one.
* **ODE instead of the closed form.** The Stan code evaluates the analytic
  solution with the infant volume frozen at each observation time; the
  packaged model integrates the mass-balanced ODEs with a time-varying infant
  volume. They are identical for constant infant weight (shown above).
* **Infant weight on CLbo.** The Stan code evaluates the infant-clearance
  covariate at the infant's average study weight (`BWT`); the packaged model
  uses the current `WT_INFANT`. With about 0.3 kg of growth on a 6 kg infant
  and an exponent of 0.55 this changes `CLbo` by up to about 1.3% at the
  start and end of the study; supply a constant `WT_INFANT` equal to the study
  average to remove it, at the cost of a constant infant volume.
* **Reference weights.** Eqs. 6-7 centre on 70 kg (mother) and 5 kg (infant),
  which the paper calls the median weights although Table 1 gives 56 kg and
  6.2-6.5 kg; the model uses 70 kg and 5 kg, as the equations do.
* **Constants held at their prior means.** The TBW coefficients and the
  milk-water, oxidation-water and atmospheric fractions are sampled from
  priors in the paper; the model and the `Rs` calculation use their means.
* **Virtual cohort.** Individual weights are not published. Maternal and
  start-of-study infant weights are drawn log-normally around the Table 1
  medians with spreads matching the interquartile ranges; every infant gains
  0.3 kg over 14 days, linearly. All pairs receive 30 g, the median dose.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found for this article (Europe
  PMC, checked 2026-11-25).
